original_value: AbstractThis paper explores the use of mobile phones to access maternal health care in sub‐Saharan Africa and whether it enhances capability and human development. Analysing focus groups and interviews on mobile phone uses by pregnant women in Nigeria based on the Technology Augmented Capability Approach, we show that the mobile phone as a technical object facilitates three broad capabilities for pregnant women, namely, (a) enhances their voice and choice to push for health care quality, (b) enhances their access to emergency services while maintaining entrepreneurial activities, and (c) enhances their health literacy and social connectedness. However, personal, social, and environmental factors influence the conversion of the use of the mobile phone into capabilities by the pregnant women.

result.paraphrase: Abstract: This paper examines how mobile phones are used to access maternal health care in sub-Saharan Africa and whether they improve capability and human development. Drawing on focus groups and interviews about how pregnant women in Nigeria use mobile phones, and using the Technology Augmented Capability Approach, we show that the phone as a technological tool supports three broad capabilities for pregnant women: (a) strengthening their voice and choice to advocate for better health-care quality, (b) improving access to emergency services while continuing entrepreneurial activities, and (c) increasing health literacy and social connectedness. However, personal, social, and environmental factors shape whether pregnant women can convert mobile phone use into capabilities.
